passages.instructions:
Questions 1–40

You should spend about 60 minutes on Questions 1–40, which are based on the reading passage below.
passages.body:
Informal Economy Measurement

A Informal economy measurement attempts to quantify economic activity outside full tax and regulatory oversight, including street vending, unregistered workshops, casual day labour, and household production not captured in standard national accounts. Motivations mix survival strategies amid weak job creation with deliberate evasion by profitable firms underreporting sales. Sizes estimated via electricity consumption gaps, currency demand approaches, and labour force surveys triangulating multiple methods because no single indicator is flawless. World Bank and IMF publications periodically revise informal share estimates affecting policy narratives about development progress and tax capacity assumptions shaping loan conditionality packages negotiated with finance ministries reliant on donor technical assistance calibrating models citizens rarely scrutinise until austerity follows

B Developing countries often exhibit larger informal shares where formal registration costs exceed benefits, corruption discourages interaction with inspectors, and social protection ties to payroll jobs unavailable. Microenterprises operate with limited capital, using family labour flexibly adjusting to demand shocks. Women dominate informal trade and home-based piecework, invisible in headline gross domestic product yet essential for household consumption smoothing. Digital payment adoption creates electronic trails partially formalising flows previously cash-only, enabling tax authorities to cross-match transactions if privacy laws permit, sparking debates about surveillance versus broadening fiscal base fairly without crushing microscopic margins sustaining urban poor majorities in rapidly urbanising continents where formal job growth lags demographic pressures youth bulges generate

C Measurement challenges include definitional boundaries: should babysitting among neighbours count, or only marketised equivalents? Agricultural subsistence blends formal and informal depending on sale proportions. Cross-country comparability suffers when statistical offices lack resources for enterprise censuses, imputing informal activity residually as discrepancy between expenditure and income sides of accounts, a fragile practice amplifying revisions startling policymakers. Satellite activities like illegal mining and drug markets pose ethical and data collection dilemmas; analysts sometimes exclude or separately estimate dark economy components using criminal justice statistics imperfectly. Environmental externalities from unregulated workshops affect health costs socialised while profits privatised, a welfare loss informal GDP additions alone do not net out without valuing pollution morbidity

D Policy responses range from crackdowns and demolitions of informal markets—often harming poorest—to facilitation programmes offering simplified registration, microfinance, and collective bargaining for home workers. Latin American associational economies legalised street vending zones with fee schedules balancing order and access. India's goods and services tax aimed to integrate supply chains digitally, burdening some small firms initially while larger formal retailers gained competitive edges exploiting input tax credits complicated for informal suppliers lacking invoices. Gradualism versus shock therapy divides reformers; sudden formalisation without support can push activity deeper underground worsening measurement and protection simultaneously, a lesson repeated after currency demonetisation experiments seeking to flush cash hoards yet disrupting trade networks overnight with

E Labour law extensions granting minimum wages and safety rules to domestic workers and platform gig couriers blur informal-formal boundaries as courts redefine employment relationships. Statistics agencies must update sampling frames including new occupational categories emerging from app-mediated work not listed in decades-old classification manuals still used in household surveys misrecording gig income as unemployment or self-employment ambiguously, distorting unemployment rates policymakers tout improving while precarity deepens hidden in heterogeneous self-employment entries requiring redesigned questionnaires piloted expensively before national rollouts feasible on tight budgets competing with health and education line items finance ministers protect more visibly than statistical modernization until crises reveal data blind spots during pandemics when informal workers lacked

F Tax administration technology—electronic invoicing, presumptive taxes for micro firms, differentiated rates—can expand base if paired with taxpayer service centres explaining obligations without extortion. Social insurance subsidies for informal workers joining voluntary schemes appear in Thailand and China experiments with mixed uptake depending on trust and benefit tangibility. Macroeconomic planners underestimating informal resilience may misforecast consumption during shocks when informal buffers absorb blows formal sectors cannot, while overestimating tax potential leads to unrealistic fiscal targets inviting procyclical austerity hurting both sectors synergistically negative. The author urges humility in estimates and participatory dialogue with informal associations co-designing reforms rather than top-down bulldozers erasing livelihoods without relocation plans or compensation funds financed progressively

G Looking ahead, better measurement supports inclusive policy if used to extend rights not only extract revenue. Satellite imagery and mobile money metadata offer new tools requiring governance safeguards. Integrating informal statistics into national accounts transparently improves credibility of growth narratives attracting investment if accompanied by legal reforms lowering formalisation costs. If measurement weaponised to stigmatise informal workers as criminals, trust will collapse undermining data quality as respondents conceal activity. Balanced formalisation recognises informal economy as ladder and lifeline, aiming to upgrade conditions while building tax capacity fairly—a developmental state task intertwining statistics, justice, and economic dignity in societies where informality is norm not exception deserving respect in policy language finally
